contracts.freshness: TTL no more than 300 seconds plus event-driven invalidation
contracts.ordering: product version wins; stale version must not replace newer version
contracts.idempotency: set by product_id and source version
contracts.rebuild: discard the namespace and repopulate from PostgreSQL
contracts.failure_mode: cache miss or cache outage falls back to bounded PostgreSQL reads
contracts.reconciliation: sample cache version and payload checksum against PostgreSQL
contracts.deletion: tombstone or version bump prevents deleted products from reappearing
contracts.security: cache stores only the approved public product projection
contracts.exit: disable cache routing and delete the derived namespace

contracts.source: transactional outbox committed with the order change
contracts.freshness: P99 publish lag target to be set in chapter 24
contracts.ordering: partition by order_id; no global order is promised
contracts.idempotency: event_id is globally stable and consumers persist processed identity
contracts.rebuild: replay retained events or regenerate an explicitly versioned state snapshot
contracts.failure_mode: database commit succeeds independently; relay retries without changing event_id
contracts.reconciliation: compare outbox published status, broker offsets, and consumer acknowledgements
contracts.deletion: privacy deletion uses a separately versioned tombstone and retention workflow
contracts.security: topic ACL separates producers, consumers, and operators
contracts.exit: drain relay, freeze offset manifest, and move consumers to an approved replacement

contracts.source: application upload workflow with PostgreSQL metadata reservation
contracts.freshness: object becomes visible only after checksum and metadata state agree
contracts.delivery: multipart or single upload with immutable object version
contracts.ordering: metadata generation number selects the active object
contracts.rebuild: object bytes are restored from versioned object backup; metadata is restored from PostgreSQL
contracts.failure_mode: orphan upload is quarantined; missing bytes never produce a successful media response
contracts.reconciliation: periodically compare object inventory, size, checksum, and PostgreSQL metadata
contracts.deletion: two-phase tombstone then retention-aware object deletion
contracts.security: private bucket, short-lived signed access, encryption and audit logging
contracts.exit: copy verified immutable versions to a replacement and atomically change metadata location

contracts.source: versioned snapshot or CDC stream from pg36_shop
contracts.freshness: batch or CDC lag is explicit on every dataset
contracts.delivery: snapshot plus ordered change stream with a source watermark
contracts.ordering: source commit position and primary key determine the latest record
contracts.idempotency: dataset version, primary key, and source commit position
contracts.rebuild: create a new dataset version from a consistent PostgreSQL snapshot and replay changes
contracts.failure_mode: stale datasets are labeled and consumers stop at the last complete watermark
contracts.reconciliation: row counts, business aggregates, and partition checksums by watermark
contracts.deletion: propagate tombstones and verify regulated deletion across retained versions
contracts.security: column classification and purpose-specific access policy
contracts.exit: freeze a final manifest and rebuild the projection in a replacement system

contracts.source: versioned product snapshot plus outbox or CDC changes
contracts.sink: external search index with explicit index generation
contracts.freshness: maximum accepted indexing lag is defined before activation
contracts.ordering: product version and deletion tombstone are monotonic
contracts.idempotency: product_id, source version, and index generation
contracts.rebuild: build a new index generation from PostgreSQL and swap an alias after golden validation
contracts.failure_mode: serve a labeled stale generation or fall back to PostgreSQL according to query class
contracts.reconciliation: quality golden, document counts, sampled payload hashes, and tombstone audit
contracts.deletion: tombstones must survive retries and index-generation swaps
contracts.security: only the approved searchable projection is exported
contracts.exit: remove routing to the external index and retain PostgreSQL search until clients drain

limitations: Component product names, credentials, endpoints, and retention periods are intentionally absent.
A contract in conditional state is not an authorization to deploy the external system.
Authority is assigned per data domain; no component is declared the universal source of truth.
Freshness text must be converted to measured SLOs and alerts in the lower volume.
